standard.title: Grammar and writing systems
standard.description: develop knowledge of, and use structures and features of, the target language grammatical and writing systems to understand and create spoken, written and multimodal texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students enter the Y7-10 sequence without formal prior knowledge of the target language grammatical system. They bring implicit grammatical knowledge from English and may have informal exposure to the target language. They have not yet learned the grammatical structures or writing system conventions of the target language.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop knowledge of and use key grammatical structures and writing system features of the target language — including word classes, agreement, verb conjugation, sentence construction and orthographic conventions — to understand and create spoken, written and multimodal texts.

nodes.label: Writing system and orthographic conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and apply the orthographic conventions of the target language writing system, including any characters, symbols or capitalization rules that differ from English.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and apply at least three orthographic conventions of the target language that differ from English (e.g. capitalisation rules, special characters, diacritics, punctuation marks).
nodes.typical_width: Apply target language orthographic conventions consistently in written production; recognise and use special characters, diacritics and punctuation marks specific to the target language; understand how these are entered on keyboards and devices.
wider: Compare capitalisation and punctuation conventions across the target language and English — create a reference resource documenting key differences
Investigate how the target language's orthographic conventions reflect its phonological system — identify where spelling reliably predicts pronunciation
nodes.hinge_reason: Orthographic accuracy is a prerequisite for written text production and comprehension. Students who do not learn target language-specific characters, diacritics or punctuation conventions produce texts that are ambiguous or incorrect, and misread texts that rely on these conventions for meaning. All subsequent writing tasks depend on this foundation.

response_modes.reason: Orthographic conventions are procedural — students typically understand the rules but apply them inconsistently, especially under text production load. Focused practice including keyboard entry, handwriting and self-correction routines builds reliable application.

success_criteria: Applies at least three target language-specific orthographic conventions correctly in written production
Can enter target language special characters or diacritics on a device when required

nodes.label: Grammatical gender and agreement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and apply grammatical gender and number agreement rules of the target language where these are grammatically required.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply gender and number agreement correctly in at least five target language phrases involving nouns and their modifiers.
nodes.typical_width: Apply gender and number agreement with nouns, articles, adjectives and possessives across spoken and written production; recognise common patterns and exceptions; use agreement rules to self-correct drafts.
wider: Research how grammatical gender is evolving in the target language (e.g. gender-neutral forms, changing norms) — compare contemporary and traditional usage
Compare grammatical gender systems across two or more languages students know — identify structural similarities and differences
nodes.hinge_reason: Gender and agreement errors propagate throughout all written and spoken production. Students who do not develop reliable agreement intuition produce texts with pervasive errors that impede comprehension and undermine all subsequent grammar nodes. EC06's text creation tasks cannot be met without basic agreement accuracy.

response_modes.reason: Agreement is procedural — errors are typically in execution rather than understanding. Focused production practice with immediate corrective feedback, including self-correction during drafting, builds reliable application.

success_criteria: Applies gender and number agreement correctly in at least five target language phrases in written production
Can identify and correct an agreement error when one is pointed out in their own writing

nodes.label: Verb conjugation and subject pronouns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and use subject pronouns and conjugate familiar verbs in the target language, including common irregular forms.
nodes.minimum_width: Conjugate at least three regular verbs correctly across at least three persons in the present tense; use subject pronouns accurately to accompany or replace nouns.
nodes.typical_width: Conjugate regular verbs across all persons in the present tense; recognise and use common irregular verb forms; use verb conjugations in affirmative, negative and interrogative forms; apply appropriate subject pronouns.
wider: Compare the verb conjugation systems of the target language and English — identify structural differences and what English omits that the target language requires
Investigate pronoun systems in the target language — map formal, informal and plural distinctions and how they reflect social relationships
nodes.hinge_reason: Verb conjugation is the structural spine of sentence production in most target languages. Students who cannot conjugate verbs reliably cannot produce grammatically complete sentences — all spoken and written production is blocked or severely impaired. This cascades directly into EC06 and EU02's more complex grammar nodes.

response_modes.reason: Conjugation accuracy requires procedural fluency — understanding the rules is not sufficient for reliable production under communicative pressure. Massed conjugation practice in meaningful production contexts (not only paradigm drills) builds the automaticity required.

Conjugation accuracy is best built through varied communicative contexts (describing routines, giving instructions, interviewing peers) rather than isolated paradigm drills. Each context activates the same rules in a different production environment.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Investigating the target language's pronoun system — particularly where it encodes social distinctions that English does not — is a concrete, grammatically-grounded entry into intercultural understanding. The grammar and the cultural insight are inseparable here.
success_criteria: Can conjugate at least three regular verbs correctly across three or more persons in the present tense
Can produce affirmative, negative and interrogative forms of a familiar verb

nodes.label: Sentence construction and connectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct grammatically coherent sentences in the target language, link ideas using connectives, and apply interrogative forms to ask questions.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least five grammatically coherent sentences in the target language using at least one connective and at least one interrogative form.
nodes.typical_width: Construct a range of sentence types (statements, questions, negatives) with appropriate word order; link ideas using connectives; use interrogative forms to gather information; apply prepositions of place and time.
wider: Compare word order conventions in the target language and English — identify where the target language requires different placement for adjectives, adverbs or objects
Investigate how connective use in the target language differs from English — identify connectives that do not have direct English equivalents

response_modes.reason: Sentence construction draws together orthographic conventions, agreement and verb conjugation from nodes 1–3 into connected text production. The teaching investment is in supporting students to maintain accuracy across multi-clause constructions, not only in isolated sentences.

success_criteria: Produces at least five grammatically coherent sentences using correct word order, agreement and verb conjugation
Uses at least one connective and at least one interrogative form correctly
